items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — jumped straight from 'how can I help you' into pricing
Never checked availability out loud for Aug 26 — just assumed and booked it
No No Worries Damage Coverage mention ($2,000) — insurance never came up at all in a call where the customer is handing over all his belongings
No Meet Your Mover email description
No On-Time Guarantee — never said Einstein discounts if it misses the arrival window
Did not use the 'pricing is super simple' framing; what's-included list was partial (blankets/shrink wrap/disassembly only — no truck, gas, insurance, taxes called out as included)
No 'does that make sense?' sense-check after the clock explanation

Save Your Ass prep speech never given — no consolidation examples (kids' toys, garden tools, loose drawer items, photos off walls), no 'take a carload' tip. Only a reactive 'anything you do brings the time down' after the customer raised it
Did not explain the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email or ask the customer to reply with corrections
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?'
Never asked how many boxes, about additional stops, storage stops, garage/storage unit/balcony, or moving stressors
Never used the customer's name — said 'sir' once, never 'Matthew'
top_strength: Gave a fast, concrete, honest estimate the customer explicitly said other movers couldn't provide, then re-quoted cleanly the moment packing entered the picture (3-4 hrs / $675-875 base, up to 6-7 hrs / $1,200-1,400 packed). His answers on loaded drawers and particle-board furniture were genuinely expert and built trust.
coaching_note: Jack is closing on product knowledge alone and leaving the whole differentiator block on the table — No Worries coverage, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee were never mentioned once. Add those three plus the Save Your Ass prep speech to every call; they cost 60 seconds and they are the reason customers pick Einstein over the cheaper quote.
phone_presence_notes: Casual and easy to talk to with light warmth ('No, I gotcha', 'Cool'), but heavy filler and repetition, zero name use, and no empathy or rapport moments beyond answering questions.
